Coram: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PRADEEP KUMAR SRIVASTAVA ------
For the Petitioner : Mr. Ashim Kr. Sahani, Advocate For the State : Mr. Sardhu Mahto, Addl.P.P ------
Order No.04 Dated- 15.03.2024 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. Apprehending his arrest in connection with Kadma P.S. Case No. 19 of 2023 instituted under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
3. As per FIR, allegation is that when the prosecutrix was an employee in a store, where she developed friendship with the petitioner.
On the promise of marriage, the petitioner established physical relationship with her several times.
When the prosecutrix asked for marriage, petitioner flatly denied to solemnize marriage with her.
Accordingly, the FIR has been registered.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.

The real fact is that the prosecutrix has developed love affairs with the petitioner and by taking advantage of the same, she lodged case and the story of establishing physical relationship between them is entirely false and fabricated.

It is further submitted that the prosecutrix has raised demand of Rs.5 lakhs from the petitioner in garb of implicating him in a false case, hence, informatory petition under section 39 of Cr.PC dated 14.02.2023 was lodged by the petitioner in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, East Singhbhum at Jamshedpur (annexure-2).

entities.text: Chief Judicial Magistrate, East Singhbhum at Jamshedpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that petitioner has also represented the matter before the Sr.S.P., Jamshedpur in the month of April, 2023 explaining the entire events.
It is further submitted that petitioner is an employee of private firm.

As per allegation made in the FIR, no offence under section 376 of IPC is constituted against the petitioner and also in view of the fact that the victim lady is a major lady and in order to squeeze the money from the petitioner, she has concocted a false story to implicate him.

Petitioner has no criminal antecedents and he undertakes to co-operate with the investigation of the case and abide all terms and conditions as Manraj Mehandi vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93878739/
1 imposed by the court.

sentences.text: Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.

5. Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner and submits that there is direct and specific allegation against the petitioner that while the petitioner was working with the victim lady, he developed intimacy with the her and in spite of her protest and willingness, the petitioner established physical relationship with her under the false pretext of marriage and he has constantly fulfilled his lust about 9 months.
When the prosecutrix asked for marriage and putting pressure upon the petitioner then he flatly declined to solemnize marriage with her.
The intention of the petitioner was dishonest and deceitful from the very inception.
In deceitful manner, he satisfied his own lust, thereafter he declined to solemnize marriage without any reasonable cause.

The allegation about demand of Rs.5 lakhs by the prosecutrix is totally baseless and fabricated story and accordingly the informatory application might have been filed by the petitioner only to save his skin from his misdeeds and the case to be lodged by the informant victim.
Hence, petitioner may not be extended privilege of anticipatory bail.

6. Considering the fact and circumstances of the case and perusal of the case diary and materials like medical report of the victim, it appears that while the prosecutrix was working with the present petitioner in a store in course of employment, both of them came into contact with each other and in the month of May, 2022 petitioner assured and induced the prosecutrix to solemnize marriage with her and against her wish and protest, petitioner indulged in sexual intercourse.
The factual aspects of the case are that from the very inception, the intention of the petitioner was dishonest and he was not sincere to keep his promise rather to satisfy his own lust.

In view of the serious and heinous nature of offence against the petitioner showing his involvement in the commission of rape under the false pretext of marriage and materials available on record, I am not inclined to extend the privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
Accordingly, the prayer of anticipatory bail of petitioner is rejected.

(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Pappu/
